action_criteria.rationale: The outside report of enlarged ventricles has no images, so an MRI must measure the ventricles, show the supportive features and exclude an obstruction before CSF is removed.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform the large-volume lumbar tap before brain MRI has excluded a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus

Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not attribute the syndrome to normal ageing or deconditioning once the ventriculomegaly and the tap response are documented
required_recommendations: Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the tap-test improvement of 36% in TUG at 24 hours, the DESH MRI (Evans index 0.38, callosal angle 72 degrees) and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery, given four falls in 6 months

avoided_actions.rationale: He has no episodes suggesting seizures, so an EEG cannot help separate iNPH from its mimics.
His falls are mechanical, with no syncope or palpitations, so an ECG does not inform the gait work-up.
There is no syncope, murmur or embolic event, so echocardiography has no role in this work-up.
An MRI is available and measures the callosal angle, temporal horns and aqueduct better than CT.
The falls are not syncopal and orthostatic testing is normal, so rhythm monitoring has no diagnostic role.
Molecular or advanced imaging does not change the iNPH decision, which rests on MRI and the tap test
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Normal-pressure CSF with a normal cell count in a two-year afebrile gait syndrome gives no indication for prion, inflammatory or infectious assays.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Only a thin Fazekas 1 periventricular halo with no deep lesions or lacunes, far less than the ventriculomegaly, and the gait improves after the tap.
Shuffling and freezing overlap, but there is no rest tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia of the arms or asymmetry, and the gait responds to CSF removal.
The memory deficit improves with cues within a dysexecutive profile, the hippocampi are MTA 1, and gait and urinary symptoms lead the syndrome.

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventricles are enlarged out of proportion to the sulci, with DESH and a callosal angle of 72 degrees, and the gait improves after the tap.

differential.diagnosis: Secondary communicating hydrocephalus (post-traumatic, post-haemorrhagic or post-meningitic)
differential.key_features: No head injury, meningitis or intracranial haemorrhage in the history.

key_clinical_evidence: Probable iNPH needs an insidious gait disturbance after age 40 lasting at least 3 to 6 months with cognitive or urinary symptoms, no antecedent cause, ventriculomegaly (Evans index greater than 0.3) not explained by atrophy, and a CSF opening pressure of 5 to 18 mmHg (7 to 24.5 cmH2O) [Relkin_2005].
DESH (tight high-convexity sulci with enlarged Sylvian fissures) and an acute callosal angle support the diagnosis; here Evans 0.38, DESH and a callosal angle of 72 degrees [Nakajima_2021].

The tap test removes 30 to 50 mL and repeats the timed gait measures at 2 to 4 and 24 hours [Nakajima_2021]; a 10% or greater TUG improvement is a commonly used positive threshold, though no guideline sets a single cut-off. Its sensitivity is 26% to 61% and its PPV 73% to 100%, so a single negative tap does not exclude shunt-responsive iNPH [Marmarou_2005].
Reversible-cause labs do not diagnose or exclude iNPH and are optional.

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]
The baseline gait must be measured before the tap, or the post-tap change cannot be interpreted [Nakajima_2021]

patient.chief_complaint: Two years of progressive shuffling gait, urinary incontinence and forgetfulness
patient.history_present_illness: A 73-year-old retired engineer with hypertension and hyperlipidemia was admitted for evaluation of two years of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence and forgetfulness. His walking has slowly worsened: he now uses a cane and has had four falls in 6 months, one causing a hip bruise. His wife describes him as 'walking like his feet are glued to the floor.' Over the same period he developed urinary urgency and incontinence; he wears pads daily and is incontinent at night. His wife reports that he frequently repeats himself, forgets recent conversations and has become slow in decision-making. An outpatient MMSE was 24/30. A brain MRI obtained by his primary care physician at an outside facility was reported as showing enlarged ventricles; the images are not available. He was referred by his primary care physician for progressive gait difficulty with memory decline and urinary incontinence. He has no resting tremor or stiffness, no lightheadedness on standing, and no history of head injury, meningitis or intracranial hemorrhage.

neurological_exam.additional: No cogwheel rigidity. No postural tremor. Pull test: 2 steps backward, recovers. No orthostatic hypotension on standing.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin mildly awkward bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Short shuffling steps on a wide base with markedly reduced foot clearance (magnetic gait). En-bloc turning. Freezing at doorways. Cannot tandem walk. Walks with a cane.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person, place, time and situation. Slowed responses. No aphasia. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength throughout. No tremor. No rigidity.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration mildly reduced at ankles (age-appropriate). Joint position intact.
